readme.content:
# interface-mcp-agent-creator

A set of Claude Code skills that explore web applications through Chrome MCP and generate TypeScript MCP tool servers from discovered features.

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

## What is this?

Most MCP tool servers are written by hand against known APIs or source code. This project flips that: it starts from the user interface. Point it at a running web application, and it explores every page, button, form, and navigation path through the browser -- no source code access required. The result is a fully generated TypeScript MCP server with one tool per discovered feature.

The project is built for developers who want to wrap existing web applications in MCP tooling without reverse-engineering the frontend codebase. It works equally well on apps you built yourself and on third-party apps where you only have a login. Multi-role exploration is supported, so you can map what an admin sees versus what a regular user sees, then generate tools scoped to each role.

Four Claude Code skills form a pipeline. Each skill reads the artifacts produced by the previous one and writes its own artifacts for the next. The pipeline is Chrome MCP agnostic -- it detects at runtime whether you have chrome-devtools-mcp, wsl-chrome-mcp, playwright-mcp, or another variant, and adapts accordingly. Generated servers use `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` for tool registration and `@mcp-ui/server` for UI content, producing only `rawHtml` and `externalUrl` content types.

## The Pipeline

```
 +----------------+     +------------------+     +-------------------+     +----------------------+
 | app-explorer   | --> | feature-mapper   | --> | code-correlator   | --> | mcp-tool-generator   |
 |                |     |                  |     |    (optional)     |     |                      |
 | Explore UI via |     | Build feature    |     | Map features to   |     | Generate TypeScript   |
 | Chrome MCP     |     | matrix by role   |     | source code       |     | MCP server           |
 +----------------+     +------------------+     +-------------------+     +----------------------+
                                            \                             /
                                             +-------- skip path --------+
                                               (1 -> 2 -> 4 supported)
```

The code-correlator skill is optional. When source code is unavailable or correlation is unnecessary, the pipeline supports going directly from feature-mapper to mcp-tool-generator.

## Skills

| Skill | Description | Trigger Phrases |
|---|---|---|
| app-explorer | BFS traversal of a web application through Chrome MCP. Discovers pages, interactive elements, and navigation paths. Supports multi-role exploration. | "explore this app", "map this application", "discover features", "crawl this web app", "what features does this app have", "explore as [role]" |
| feature-mapper | Transforms exploration data into structured feature documentation organized by user role. Produces a feature matrix with role-based access details. | "document features", "map features by role", "create feature matrix", "what can each role do", "compare user roles", "feature documentation" |
| code-correlator | Maps UI features to their source code locations -- component files, handler functions, and related code. Optional: pipeline can skip this skill. | "find feature in code", "map UI to code", "where is this button in the code", "correlate interface to source", "find component for", "test this feature" |
| mcp-tool-generator | Generates a complete TypeScript MCP server with one tool per feature. Uses `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` and `@mcp-ui/server`. | "generate MCP tools", "create frontend MCP", "build MCP server", "create tools for this app", "generate mcp-ui tools", "build tool server" |

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) installed and configured
- Any Chrome MCP variant connected (chrome-devtools-mcp, wsl-chrome-mcp, playwright-mcp, or similar)

### Manual install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/477174/interface-mcp-agent-creator.git
cp -r interface-mcp-agent-creator/.claude/skills/* your-project/.claude/skills/
```

The skills will be available in Claude Code the next time you start a session in that project.

## Usage

### Step 1: Explore the application

```
Explore https://myapp.example.com as admin and as viewer
```

The app-explorer skill will navigate every reachable page, record interactive elements, and save exploration artifacts to `.claude/artifacts/exploration-{timestamp}/`.

### Step 2: Map features by role

```
Create a feature matrix from the exploration
```

The feature-mapper skill reads the exploration output and produces a structured feature map with per-role access details, saved to `.claude/artifacts/feature-map-{timestamp}/`.

### Step 3 (optional): Correlate to source code

```
Map UI features to source code
```

If your application source code is available locally, the code-correlator skill maps each feature to component files and handler functions. Output goes to `.claude/artifacts/code-map-{timestamp}/`. Skip this step if source code is unavailable.

### Step 4: Generate the MCP server

```
Generate MCP tools for this app
```

The mcp-tool-generator skill reads the feature map (and optionally the code map) and generates a complete TypeScript MCP server with one tool per feature, saved to `.claude/artifacts/mcp-server-{timestamp}/`.

## Output

Each skill writes artifacts to a timestamped directory under `.claude/artifacts/`:

| Skill | Artifact Directory | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| app-explorer | `exploration-{timestamp}/` | Pages, elements, navigation edges, role-separated files for multi-role runs |
| feature-mapper | `feature-map-{timestamp}/` | Feature entries with IDs, categories, actions, role access, and role comparison data |
| code-correlator | `code-map-{timestamp}/` | Feature-to-source mappings with component files, handler functions, confidence levels |
| mcp-tool-generator | `mcp-server-{timestamp}/` | Complete TypeScript MCP server project with one tool per feature |

The generated MCP server uses two content types:

- **rawHtml** -- inline HTML for form confirmations, action status, compact tables, and small result panes.
- **externalUrl** -- iframe-based URL rendering for dashboards, full-page workflows, and complex interactive views.

## Validation

Three shell scripts under `scripts/` verify skill integrity:

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `validate-format.sh` | Checks all 4 skills against the Anthropic skill specification: frontmatter structure, word count limits, kebab-case naming, no stray README.md files, and references/ directory presence. |
| `validate-no-hardcoded-tools.sh` | Scans all skill files for hardcoded Chrome MCP tool prefixes. Skills must detect the Chrome MCP variant at runtime, never assume a specific one. |
| `validate-output-contracts.sh` | Verifies each skill has its output or input format reference file, ensuring the artifact contract between pipeline stages is documented. |

Run all three from the repository root:

```bash
bash scripts/validate-format.sh
bash scripts/validate-no-hardcoded-tools.sh
bash scripts/validate-output-contracts.sh
```
